details.body: In conservation_regression.rs, the grazing test (closed_system_grazing_conserves_n_and_c, lines 257-271) still uses bare `assert!()` for pathway verification instead of the new `assert_or_dump()` helper that all other five tests use. This means a grazing pathway assertion failure will NOT dump the trace to /tmp/tank_conservation_traces/grazing.jsonl, violating the acceptance criterion that 'failures dump the full trace to a file for debugging.' Replace the three bare `assert!()` calls with `assert_or_dump("grazing", &engine, ...)` calls.

In e2e_conservation.rs, `run_grazing()` (lines 375-390) has no pathway-verification assertions (ensure/ensure_trace_delta), while all other five scenario runners (run_feeding, run_mortality_senescence, run_trim_and_remove, run_trim_and_leave, run_water_change) were enhanced with these checks in this diff. Add at minimum: ensure that periphyton decreased, TAN increased, and fine detritus increased (mirroring the unit test), so the e2e runner catches the case where grazing is silently not exercised.

In the water-change test (both files), the expected_n_import calculation only sums `source.ammonia_mg_n_per_l + source.nitrate_mg_n_per_l + source.don_mg_n_per_l`, omitting `source.nitrite_mg_n_per_l`. The engine's budget (apply_water_change_with_budget, line 125-128) sums all four source species including nitrite. This only works because the source profile's nitrite is implicitly zero from SourceWaterProfile::zero(). Add `+ source.nitrite_mg_n_per_l` to the test's expected_n_import formula for correctness and resilience against fixture evolution.

Align the shipped default process preset with the new named stoichiometric constant. `ProcessParams::default()` now uses `NITRIFICATION_ALK_MEQ_PER_MG_N` in `crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:337-338`, but the runtime default preset loaded from `crates/tank_data/data/process/default.toml:52-54` still hard-codes `0.1428`, and scenario startup converts that preset into live params in `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:346-349`. As written, two code paths that both claim to use the default process parameters will consume different alkalinity and can diverge in deterministic comparisons.

Fix alkalinity assertion messages to use `meq` consistently. `crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:471-476` and `crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:494-507` still hard-code `mg` in the per-system and per-stage lines, so a failing `Element::Alkalinity` assertion prints the wrong unit even though the headline/before-after lines were updated to `meq`.

The 6 conservation test fixtures in `conservation_regression.rs` are copied verbatim into `e2e_conservation.rs` (grazing_fixture, feeding_fixture, mortality_senescence_fixture, trim_fixture, water_change_fixture, plus helpers close_gas_exchange, disable_dic_shortcuts, dump_trace). Extract shared fixtures into a `test_fixtures` module (e.g. `crates/tank_core/tests/common/conservation_fixtures.rs`) or a `#[cfg(test)]` module in tank_core that both test files import. This prevents silent divergence when a fixture is updated in one file but not the other.

Test 3 (`closed_system_mortality_senescence_conserves_n_and_c`) verifies trace evidence for plant senescence → detritus and algae senescence → detritus, but does not verify shrimp death → detritus via an explicit `assert_trace_delta` for `system:daily_shrimp` / `detritus.fine_g`. Add a trace assertion that shrimp death routes biomass to fine detritus, matching the doc comment's claim that 'shrimp death and plant senescence route biomass to detritus.'
